audit: Second independent read-only max review of current uncommitted assistant remediation

evidence.method: Current built actual HttpModelProvider/Application/Engine/Vault + loopback synthetic HTTP service + in-memory SQLite; no ScriptedModelProvider, paid model, real credential or production DB.

findings.title: The new server intent envelope still turns common explicit negatives into authorization
findings.trigger: Compose request 请勿运行当前流程 or 我不想运行当前流程; 不需要发布当前流程.
findings.observed: Shared classifier returns run, run, publish respectively. Both frontend and the new server envelope accept that result. Actual HTTP provider proposed workflow_start(selected); task completed with a real synthetic run despite 请勿运行. Original 不要发布或执行 and 试运行 examples now correctly reject run.
findings.impact: The intended no-execution boundary remains bypassable by ordinary negative Chinese wording; service-side reuse of the same incomplete regex does not repair that boundary.
findings.minimumFix: Recognize negative modalities such as 勿/请勿/不想/不希望/不需要/不应/不应该 before extracting actions, or require a demonstrable affirmative verb clause; preserve quoted/examples and coordinated-negative handling. Keep positive combined commands supported without adding approvals.
findings.tests: Full real HTTP task for every negative phrase above, including exact selected workflow, malicious run/publish response; assert tool absent and no writes/runs. Add affirmative counterpart coverage.

findings.title: Clearing or switching selected run does not remove the previous run's business answer from model history
findings.trigger: Use a real session to explain selected run A; the model returns actual run A outputs. Reuse the session after clearing run context and ask a plain project-help question, optionally selecting a different model profile/provider.
findings.observed: The script performed a real analysis producing RUN_A_SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_RESULT, selected that run and received a model answer from its actual outputs. The next context={} help request still transmits the prior run-specific answer in messages history. There is no message task/context linkage or context-aware filter. UI source text currently says only current selection/help sources.
findings.impact: Old business evidence crosses the newly selected external-model context despite the run no longer being selected, and can be sent to a different provider. Existing source/context summary does not disclose this scope expansion.
findings.minimumFix: Persist taskId and context provenance on messages. Construct provider history from the selected workflow/run/artifact scope plus safe conversation turns, and omit or explicitly rescope former run evidence when selection/provider changes. Do not globally redact business content.
findings.tests: Real HTTP provider A receives selected A, then clear/switch to B and select provider B using the same session; assert the A evidence is absent unless A is explicitly selected again.

findings.title: Fresh assistant-message copies survive cleanup of their expired source run because messages are not linked to taskId
findings.trigger: Explain run A and persist a recent answer containing A's output. Make the synthetic terminal run older than seven days, preview and commit retention now.
findings.observed: Actual commitRetention marks source run resultsExpiredAt=true and selected assistant task resultsExpiredAt=true. All four real messages in the reused session have no taskId; recent assistant text containing RUN_A_SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_RESULT remains unchanged after cleanup. The preview's resultTasks.has(message.taskId) never matches actual message records.
findings.impact: The new lifecycle cleanup removes source output/task/SSE copies but leaves an ordinary message copy that can immediately be retransmitted through R02, violating the original result retention boundary.
findings.minimumFix: Write taskId to both user and assistant messages, including any analysis messages; make cleanup/context provenance cover historical records and subsequent summaries of an expired result. Coordinate with persistence remediation rather than only ageing message.createdAt independently.
findings.tests: Use actual Application.submit-generated message records, not manually taskId-tagged fixtures. Source run ages out while answer was just created; after commit assert marker absent from run/messages/tasks/tool receipts/events and future provider context, while unrelated fresh conversation remains.

findings.title: Sending a new message leaves the previous COMPLETED task visible and cancellable until acceptance returns
findings.trigger: Reuse a session with a completed task, then send a new create request with delayed POST acceptance.
findings.observed: send sets submitting but retains task/taskRef pointing at the previous COMPLETED task until the POST returns. It continues to render 任务：COMPLETED and, because busy is true and task exists, exposes a cancel button aimed at the old task. The root's actual /tmp/flowhub-v2-audit-ui.log ends 26/27, with the v2-upgrade test seeing COMPLETED then fetching the newly requested workflow before it exists (404). SSE follow-up GET handlers also setTask(next) with only a live flag, without rechecking session/task identity after await.
findings.impact: The current request is falsely presented as complete, users can open stale receipts and cancellation can target the wrong task. Out-of-order old task queries can replace the new task or selected session's task.
findings.minimumFix: Represent a separate submitting acceptance state and clear/archive the old active task before POST. Bind all SSE/status continuations to session and request/task generation. Expose cancel only for the current accepted task, and reconcile cancellation if requested before acceptance.
findings.tests: Delay message POST; verify no current COMPLETED and no stale cancel/receipt while awaiting acceptance. Delay an old SSE status response across new send/session switch and ensure it cannot overwrite current task. Await actual new taskId before workflow persistence assertions.

findings.title: Analysis ignores the newly configurable correction-attempt budget
findings.trigger: Configure model limits.maxCorrectionAttempts=1, then analyze an actual waiting checkpoint while loopback provider returns invalid JSON.
findings.observed: Actual HTTP call count is 3 and task ends INPUT_INVALID. Analysis still loops attempt<3 and does not consult the profile's maxCorrectionAttempts setting; compose-tool errors do use it.
findings.impact: A user-selected lower analysis correction/cost budget is exceeded, despite the formal profile UI/API advertising the shared setting.
findings.minimumFix: Resolve and apply the selected profile's correction-attempt limit in analyzeCheckpoint, with one total task deadline and usage accounting; distinguish an invalid initial attempt and correction rounds consistently with the compose path.
findings.tests: Profiles with limits 1/2/3 and always-invalid or eventually-valid JSON; assert exact bounded HTTP calls, usage totals, unchanged checkpoint on exhaustion, and no unwanted advance.

Server injects token into authorized advance; source strips root checkpoint credentials from receipts and scans known credentials in nested serialized context/history. Historical business selection scope remains R02.
Deleting real normal/analysis sessions now removes their task events and analysis ledger; cancellation workers prevent deletion until settled. Lifecycle interaction still has R03.
Same analysis key returns original completed acceptance after run SUCCEEDED; no reanalysis.
Real loopback text/tools probes pass and stream fails; formal assistant now falls back nonstream and completes. Profile source invalidates capabilities on identity/key change.
Headers-then-body stall now returns typed MODEL_TIMEOUT; source wraps body/SSE reads and limits nonstream 4 MiB. Retry-After bounded/cancellable path is present.

Source resets by checkpoint/run, subscribes task state, exposes errors/retry/cancel. Root actual UI log confirms analysis retry and next-checkpoint test passed; this audit did not independently rerun browser suite.
Actual source-range hash now matches the tool citation; source viewer and cursor history are implemented.

Source adds configurable compose limits, additive usage with unknown flag, history paging, task idempotency tombstone guards, stop/drain guards, and active/cancelling session deletion protection. R04 and R05 are the remaining concrete gaps found.
Source now rotates encrypted V2 provider continuations and legacy encrypted receipt credentials; no live rotation scenario rerun in this short pass.
